What is the probability you have the disease? Give the numerical answer and identify the assumption in the wording most likely to fail in practice.
log.b:
The conventional answer is 13/27, assuming independent, equally likely sexes and weekdays, and conditioning uniformly on families with at least one Tuesday-born boy. Of 27 qualifying sex/day configurations, 13 contain two boys. But the sampling protocol matters: if a randomly selected child is observed to be a Tuesday-born boy, the other child’s sex remains independent, giving 1/2. A parent’s spontaneous statement can produce still other probabilities depending on their reporting rule.
